issues.t: Cruise control deactivation switch can overheat and burn (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning. Some owners notice a burning smell, smoke near the brake master cylinder, or cruise control that stops working.
issues.why: A pressure switch on the brake master cylinder that cancels cruise control can leak brake fluid inside itself and overheat. It can start a fire under the hood even with the truck parked and switched off. Ford recalled many Rangers from these years.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the switch fixed right away. Until then, park outside and away from buildings, and stop driving if you smell burning.

issues.t: Cruise control cable can hold the throttle open (recall)
issues.sym: The engine keeps revving or the truck does not slow down when you lift off the gas pedal.
issues.why: The cruise control cable could be routed or assembled so it keeps the throttle from snapping back to idle. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the throttle ever sticks, shift to Neutral, brake firmly, and have the truck towed in rather than driving it.

issues.t: Fuel rail O-ring can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw gasoline smell under the hood or in the cab, or wet spots around the fuel injector rail.
issues.why: An O-ring at a fuel rail joint could be damaged during assembly and let fuel seep out near hot engine parts, which is a fire risk. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Do not drive if you smell fuel. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the fuel rail joints inspected.

issues.t: Chirp or squeal from the camshaft synchronizer
issues.sym: A bird-like chirp or squeal from the back of the engine, sometimes with oil seeping at the synchronizer or a check engine light.
issues.why: The bushing inside the camshaft synchronizer runs dry and wears out. Left alone, the worn part can damage its drive gear and upset ignition timing.
issues.next: Have the synchronizer replaced soon. Caught early it is a fairly simple job, and replacing it prevents damage to the gear that drives it.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle (4.0L SOHC)
issues.sym: A metallic rattle at cold start or around 2,000 to 3,000 RPM, rough running, and sometimes a check engine light.
issues.why: The plastic timing chain guides and tensioners on this engine wear or break, letting the long timing chains go slack and slap. The rear chain is hard to reach, so repairs are big jobs.
issues.next: Have it diagnosed soon and avoid hard driving until it is. If a chain jumps teeth or breaks, the engine can be badly damaged.

issues.t: Plastic thermostat housing leaks (4.0L SOHC)
issues.sym: Coolant drips or crusty residue at the front center of the engine, a sweet coolant smell, low coolant, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The thermostat housing on this engine is plastic and tends to crack or leak at its seals with age and heat. Some owners replace it more than once.
issues.next: Top up coolant and have the housing replaced with a quality part. Do not keep driving if the gauge climbs toward hot.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or harsh shifts (5R55E)
issues.sym: Slipping, harsh engagement into Drive or Reverse, a delay before Reverse engages, or the engine flaring between gears.
issues.why: The 5-speed automatic used in many Rangers is known for wear in its internal bands, servos and valve body, often made worse by old fluid.
issues.next: Have the fluid and stored codes checked early. Some problems can be fixed with smaller repairs if caught before the transmission is badly worn.

issues.t: Hood latch striker can crack (recall)
issues.sym: A loose or rattling hood, or a hood that does not stay firmly latched.
issues.why: The hood striker could fatigue and break, which may let the hood fly open while driving and block your view. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the striker replaced. Do not drive at speed if the hood feels loose.

issues.t: Front seat belt buckle may not latch fully (recall)
issues.sym: The seat belt tongue may seem to click in but pull back out.
issues.why: Some front outboard buckles could fail to latch completely, so the belt might not hold in a crash. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the buckle replaced. Tug on the belt after buckling to make sure it is locked.

issues.t: Rear differential case can crack (FX4 recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or grinding from the rear axle, or gear oil leaking from the differential.
issues.why: On some FX4 trucks with a manual transmission, the rear differential case could fracture, which can lock or disable the rear axle. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Stop driving and have the truck towed if the rear axle starts grinding or leaking heavily.

issues.t: Frame flange could puncture fuel tank in a side crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in normal driving.
issues.why: A frame flange near the fuel tank could puncture the tank in certain side impacts, raising fire risk after a crash. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the remedy installed.

issues.t: Takata air bag inflators, some under do-not-drive warnings
issues.sym: No warning before a failure. An air bag light is not a reliable sign.
issues.why: Takata inflators in these trucks can rupture in a crash and throw metal fragments. Ford told owners of certain 2004-2006 Rangers not to drive them until repaired, and later added some 2009-2011 trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls today. If an air bag recall is open, do not drive the truck. Ask the dealer to tow it or come to you.

issues.t: Turn signals, brake lights or hazards can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: Turn signals, hazard flashers or brake lights work on and off or not at all, often in hot weather.
issues.why: A plastic slider inside the multi-function switch on the steering column can soften and deform, breaking the circuit for the exterior lights. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the switch replaced. Until then, check that your brake lights work before driving, since following drivers may not see you stop.

issues.t: Windshield wiper motor can fail (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers slow down, stop partway, or quit entirely.
issues.why: Some wiper motors were built without enough grease on an internal gear, which can wear and stop the wipers. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the motor replaced. Do not drive in rain or snow if the wipers are not working.

issues.t: Front wheel spindle can crack (4x2 recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or knock from a front wheel, steering that feels loose, or a wheel that leans.
issues.why: On some two-wheel-drive trucks a front spindle could fracture, which can let a wheel separate from the suspension. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls right away. If you hear a clunk from the front end or steering feels odd, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Parking brake cable can come loose in cold weather (recall)
issues.sym: The parking brake lever feels slack or the truck rolls with the parking brake set.
issues.why: On some trucks with a manual transmission, the parking brake cable could disconnect in cold temperatures, so the truck may roll when parked. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Leave the truck in gear and chock the wheels on slopes until the cable is fixed.

issues.t: Fuel line can rub through near the throttle body (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell under the hood or wet spots on the fuel line.
issues.why: A fuel line could chafe against the throttle body heat shield and wear a hole, leaking fuel near hot parts. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Do not drive if you smell fuel. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the line inspected and fixed.

issues.t: Harsh or delayed 10-speed shifts
issues.sym: Clunky shifts at low speed, a delay engaging Drive or Reverse, shudder pulling away, or a check engine light with transmission codes.
issues.why: The 10-speed automatic can shift poorly because of control software, sticking valves in the valve body, or a clutch cylinder sleeve that can move. Ford released a service bulletin with repairs.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer to check for bulletin 23-2350 and software updates. Get it looked at sooner if the truck slips or will not engage a gear.

issues.t: HVAC blower motor can short out (recall)
issues.sym: The fan stops or works on and off, or there is a burning smell from the vents.
issues.why: The blower motor can short internally and overheat, a fire risk. Some replacement motors used in the first fix had the same problem, so Ford issued a second recall.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls, including the follow-up campaign. Stop using the fan and have it checked if you smell burning.

issues.t: Gear selector may not match the actual gear (recalls)
issues.sym: The shifter can move out of Park without your foot on the brake, or the gear shown does not match the gear the transmission is in.
issues.why: Several recalls covered a shift interlock fault, loose shifter cable bracket fasteners, and an unseated shift cable clip. Any of these can let the truck roll or move in an unexpected direction.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Always set the parking brake when parked, and do not drive the truck if the selector and the gear do not match.

issues.t: Tail lights can go out (recall)
issues.sym: Tail lights or rear lamps work on and off or not at all, sometimes with a bulb-out warning.
issues.why: Loose rear lamp connectors can lose contact, so other drivers may not see the truck at night. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the connectors repaired. Have someone confirm the rear lights work before driving at night.

issues.t: Front passenger seat belt assembly problems (recalls)
issues.sym: The passenger belt may look twisted or routed oddly, or may not hold properly.
issues.why: Some passenger seat belts were misrouted or assembled incorrectly at the factory, which can reduce protection in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the belt inspected and fixed.

issues.t: Backup camera goes blank, distorted or stuck (recalls)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture is blank, flipped, distorted, or stays on after you shift out of Reverse.
issues.why: Software errors and poor camera connections caused several recalls on this generation.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the software or camera fixed. Check mirrors carefully when backing up until then.

issues.t: Engine block heater can crack and short (recall)
issues.sym: Coolant seeping near the heater, a tripped outlet or breaker, or a burning smell when the truck is plugged in.
issues.why: The factory block heater can crack, leak coolant, and short circuit while plugged in, which is a fire risk. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Stop plugging in the block heater and check your VIN for open recalls. Have it repaired before using it again.

issues.t: Front radar may be misaligned (recall)
issues.sym: Adaptive cruise or collision warning acts oddly, shuts off, or shows a sensor warning.
issues.why: The front radar module could be mounted out of alignment, which can make adaptive cruise and automatic emergency braking work poorly. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the radar aligned. Do not rely on driver-assist features until it is fixed.

issues.t: Fuel line connection can loosen and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or fuel drips under the truck.
issues.why: A fuel line connection may not be fully seated and can leak fuel, a fire risk. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Do not drive if you smell fuel. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the connection fixed.

issues.t: Windshield may not be fully bonded (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise, creaking, or a windshield that seems to shift at the edges.
issues.why: The windshield may not have been properly bonded to the body, so it may not stay in place in a crash. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the windshield inspected and rebonded.

issues.t: Cracked engine block (2.3L EcoBoost program)
issues.sym: Low coolant warnings, coolant leaking on the right side of the engine, or the engine running hot.
issues.why: A damaged casting tool at the engine plant may have left a crack in the right side of some blocks built in spring 2023. Ford covers it with a customer satisfaction program that replaces the engine's long block.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer whether your VIN is in program 23B42. Stop driving if the engine overheats or keeps losing coolant.

issues.t: Driver-side lug nuts may be loose (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: A clicking or clunking from a wheel, or a wobble at speed.
issues.why: Lug nuts on the driver side of some trucks may not have been tightened properly at the factory, so a wheel could come off. Ford told owners not to drive until repaired.
issues.next: Do not drive the truck until it has been checked. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the dealer tow it or come to you.

issues.t: Front upper control arm ball joint nut loose or missing (recalls)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front suspension, wandering, or steering that feels loose.
issues.why: The nut that holds the upper ball joint to the steering knuckle may be missing or not tightened, which can let the control arm separate and cause loss of steering control. Ford recalled affected trucks twice.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls right away. Stop driving and have it towed if you hear clunking from the front or steering feels loose.

issues.t: Transmission may not engage Reverse or may creep (recall)
issues.sym: The truck will not back up, or it creeps forward while in Reverse or Neutral.
issues.why: The 10-speed transmission's valve body may have been machined incorrectly, which can cause loss of Reverse or unexpected movement. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Always set the parking brake and do not drive it if it moves unexpectedly in Neutral or Reverse.

issues.t: Fuel leaks from vapor line or high-pressure pump (recalls)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell around the truck, especially near the engine bay.
issues.why: Two recalls cover this year: a loose bracket can let the fuel vapor line rub through, and bolts on the high-pressure fuel pump may be loose. Both can leak fuel and raise fire risk.
issues.next: Do not drive if you smell fuel. Check your VIN for open recalls and have both fixes done.

issues.t: Power windows may not reverse on an obstruction (recalls)
issues.sym: A window closing automatically does not stop or back off when it meets a hand or object.
issues.why: The automatic close feature may not detect an obstruction, which can pinch fingers or arms. Ford issued two recalls.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Keep children's hands clear of windows and avoid one-touch close until it is fixed.

issues.t: Backup camera image delayed or frozen (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture appears late, freezes, or drops out while reversing.
issues.why: A software error can disrupt the rearview camera image. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the software updated. Use mirrors and look behind you when backing up.

issues.t: Side curtain air bags can tear when they deploy (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in normal driving.
issues.why: A curtain air bag can catch on a sharp reinforcement edge inside the door pillar and tear, losing pressure in a crash. Ford recalled trucks built before late July 2025.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the repair done promptly.

issues.t: Sun visor or headliner wiring can short (recall)
issues.sym: Visor lights or overhead features act up, or a burning smell from the headliner area.
issues.why: Wiring at the sun visor or headliner may be damaged during assembly and can short, which is a fire risk. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you smell burning or see smoke from the ceiling, stop and turn the truck off.

issues.t: Front seat height-adjust bolt can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: The seat rocks, clunks, or feels loose when you shift your weight.
issues.why: A pivot bolt in the seat height adjuster may loosen or fall out, so the seat may not hold you properly in a crash. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the seat inspected soon.

issues.t: Trailer module can lose communication (recall)
issues.sym: Trailer brake or trailer light warnings, or trailer lights and brakes that stop working.
issues.why: The trailer module may lose communication with the truck, which can disable trailer lights and electric brakes. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and avoid towing until it is repaired.

issues.t: Electronic brake booster can lose power assist (recalls)
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly feels hard and the truck takes more effort and distance to stop, often with a warning message.
issues.why: The electronic brake booster can lose its power assist because of a software or hardware fault. Ford issued two recalls for these trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls now. If the pedal goes hard, press much harder, leave extra room, and have the truck checked before driving further.

issues.t: Air bag, seat and dash assembly recalls
issues.sym: A dash that shows the wrong gauges or warnings, a driver seat that feels loose, or no symptoms at all.
issues.why: Several build problems were recalled for this year: a dash cover that can block the passenger air bag, a misconfigured instrument panel that can hide warning lights, and loose or missing driver seat frame bolts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have every open fix done before relying on the truck.

issues.t: Windshield may not be fully bonded on 2025 models (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise, creaking, or a windshield that seems to move at the edges.
issues.why: The windshield may not have been bonded to the body correctly, so it may not stay in place in a crash. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the windshield inspected.

issues.t: EGR valve failure can cut engine power (recall)
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough running, or a sudden loss of power.
issues.why: The EGR valve may fail and put the engine into a reduced-power state. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the engine loses power, pull over safely and have the truck checked before driving on.

issues.t: Internal engine failure can cause loss of power (recalls)
issues.sym: Engine knocking, warning lights, or a sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: Ford recalled certain trucks whose engines may fail, with a replacement long block as the remedy. A separate 2026 recall covers defective piston domes that can also cause loss of power.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls now. If you hear knocking or the engine loses power, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Center screen can lose power, no backup camera (recall)
issues.sym: The center touchscreen goes dark and the rear camera image does not appear in Reverse.
issues.why: The center display can lose power, which takes the rearview camera with it. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have it repaired. Use mirrors and look behind you when backing up.
